function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

message.content:
Below is a quick “starter kit” for getting startup statistics from a few popular public APIs.  
Feel free to pick the one that best fits your needs and replace the placeholder values (API keys, query parameters, etc.) with your own.

---

## 1. Crunchbase Public Data (requires API key)

Crunchbase offers a rich dataset of companies, funding rounds, and more.  
You’ll need an API key (free tier available).

```python
import requests

url = "https://api.crunchbase.com/v3.1/odm-organizations"
headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_CRUNCHBASE_API_KEY",
    "Accept": "application/json"
}
params = {
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 10,
    "organization_types": "company",
    "sort_order": "raised_amount_usd_desc"
}

response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)
data = response.json()
print(data)
```

**Example `requests_get` call (tool syntax)**

```json
{
  "name": "requests_get",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://api.crunchbase.com/v3.1/odm-organizations",
    "headers": {
      "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_CRUNCHBASE_API_KEY",
      "Accept": "application/json"
    },
    "params": {
      "page": 1,
      "per_page": 10,
      "organization_types": "company",
      "sort_order": "raised_amount_usd_desc"
    }
  }
}
```

---

## 2. AngelList GraphQL API

AngelList provides a GraphQL endpoint that lets you query companies, jobs, and more.  
No API key is required for public data, but you can add a token for higher rate limits.

```graphql
query {
  companies(first: 10, sort: "raised_amount") {
    nodes {
      name
      website
      raisedAmount
      foundedAt
      industry
    }
  }
}
```

**Example `requests_get` call (tool syntax)**

```json
{
  "name": "requests_get",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://api.angel.co/graphql",
    "headers": {
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
      "Accept": "application/json"
    },
    "params": {
      "query": "{\"query\":\"query { companies(first: 10, sort: \\\"raised_amount\\\") { nodes { name website raisedAmount foundedAt industry } } }\"}"
    }
  }
}
```

*(Note: For GraphQL you normally POST the query; the above is a workaround for the `requests_get` tool.)*

---

## 3. Startup Genome API (public endpoint)

Startup Genome offers a simple REST API for company data.  
No authentication is required for basic queries.

```python
import requests

url = "https://api.startupgenome.com/v1/companies"
params = {
    "location": "San Francisco",
    "industry": "Technology",
    "limit": 20
}

response = requests.get(url, params=params)
data = response.json()
print(data)
```

**Example `requests_get` call (tool syntax)**

```json
{
  "name": "requests_get",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://api.startupgenome.com/v1/companies",
    "params": {
      "location": "San Francisco",
      "industry": "Technology",
      "limit": 20
    }
  }
}
```

---

## 4. Generic “Startup Stats” Endpoint (placeholder)

If you have a custom or third‑party service that exposes startup statistics, you can call it like this:

```python
import requests

url = "https://api.startupstats.com/v1/companies"
params = {
    "country": "US",
    "status": "active",
    "sort": "funding_amount",
    "limit": 50
}

response = requests.get(url, params=params)
data = response.json()
print(data)
```

**Example `requests_get` call (tool syntax)**

```json
{
  "name": "requests_get",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://api.startupstats.com/v1/companies",
    "params": {
      "country": "US",
      "status": "active",
      "sort": "funding_amount",
      "limit": 50
    }
  }
}
```

---

### How to Choose

| API | Strengths | Limitations |
|-----|-----------|-------------|
| **Crunchbase** | Detailed funding data, company profiles, events | Requires API key, rate limits |
| **AngelList** | Real‑time job listings, startup profiles | Limited to public data, GraphQL complexity |
| **Startup Genome** | Geographic & industry filters, free | Smaller dataset, no authentication |
| **Custom/Third‑Party** | Tailored data, no auth if public | Depends on provider |

Pick the one that matches your data needs and integrate it into your application. If you need help with authentication or pagination, let me know!
